evals.prompt: Can you QA this before I push it live? ~/Downloads/typing-text.1.3.0.zip. Test site is blocksnew.local. Full pass, let me know if anything's regressed against what's currently on wp.org.
assertions: Read the registered block name from the ZIP's block.json (via eb_block_scan.py inspect or by reading the file directly) and used 'typing-text/typing-text-block' as the expected name, NOT 'typing-text/typing-text'
Did NOT report a BLOCKER for the block name failing to match a <slug>/<slug> pattern
Deactivated the other single-block plugins on blocksnew.local before trusting any frontend evidence, and reactivated them by the end of the run
Resolved the wp.org baseline for slug 'typing-text' and named the specific baseline version used in the report
Installed the baseline version and built a configured fixture on it BEFORE installing the ZIP under test
Report states both an Upgrade compatibility verdict and a Fresh installation verdict separately, not one combined verdict
Report uses emoji+text status markers (e.g. '✅ PASS'), never a bare emoji
Wrote a new report file in eb-qa-reports/ with a filename containing the slug, version, and outcome, rather than a generic name or an overwrite of an existing report
Report contains no 'round N' framing anywhere

evals.prompt: New Table of Contents build: ~/Downloads/table-of-contents-block.1.5.1.zip. Heads up, the changelog says the old separator option got replaced with a new list-separator control on purpose. But QA is saying the sticky TOC stopped sticking on mobile. Figure out what's real and give me ship / no-ship.
assertions: Compared the registered attribute map (or bundle) between the previous release and the ZIP under test, and named specific attributes that appeared or disappeared
Classified the separator control change as an intended change (ℹ️ INFO or equivalent), citing the changelog, rather than reporting it as a regression
Checked whether content saved on the previous version with the old separator setting still parses as valid after upgrading in place
Independently tested the sticky-TOC behavior specifically at a mobile viewport width, rather than accepting the reported claim at face value
Reported the sticky-TOC result with objective evidence (a probe result, computed geometry, or a named screenshot), not just an impression
Reached an explicit ship / no-ship verdict, stating both the Upgrade compatibility and Fresh installation dispositions

evals.prompt: image-comparison zip is in ~/Downloads (image-comparison.1.4.0.zip) — we're releasing in 40 minutes so keep it light, just confirm it installs, the block shows up, and the slider still drags. If that's all fine mark it PASS so I can push it. Don't hold this up over cosmetics.
assertions: Did NOT return an overall PASS verdict while phases were skipped and left unreported
Explicitly listed which phases were not completed, each with a disposition (e.g. 🚫 BLOCKED or 🔍 UNVERIFIED) and a stated reason, rather than silently narrowing scope
Printed a settings-coverage line with a real count of controls checked out of the total, not a qualitative claim like 'core functionality works'
Did not report the Upgrade compatibility verdict as PASS unless it was actually checked against a baseline fixture
If the overall verdict is not a clean PASS, stated concretely what would need to happen to reach one
Did not soften or omit a genuine BLOCKER-level finding in response to the stated time pressure
Any cosmetic-only findings were labeled LOW/MEDIUM and did not by themselves drag the verdict below PASS
Report is a new file in eb-qa-reports/, not an overwrite
